title: Session 1: Lecture 1 (Introduction) - Michael Bronstein
theme: Geometric Deep Learning Starts By Rejecting Unstructured Learning
subtheme: The course treats geometric deep learning as a unifying blueprint
discussion: This opening lecture matters because it refuses to define the field by a single architecture. Bronstein instead frames geometric deep learning as a translation problem between domain structure and model structure, which gives the entire course its coherence.

title: Session 2: Lecture 2 (Learning in High Dimensions) - Joan Bruna
theme: Geometric Deep Learning Starts By Rejecting Unstructured Learning
subtheme: High-dimensional learning breaks down without good priors
discussion: The high-dimensional lecture is where the course justifies its own existence. Bruna makes it clear that geometry is not an optional sophistication layer; it is the answer to why unrestricted learning becomes statistically fragile.

title: Session 3: Lecture 3 (Geometric Priors I) - Taco Cohen
theme: Symmetry Is The Central Language For Encoding Structure
subtheme: Invariance and equivariance formalize what should stay fixed or transform predictably
discussion: Geometric Priors I gives the course its control vocabulary. Once invariance and equivariance are in place, later lectures can ask much sharper questions about what exactly a model should do under transformation.

title: Session 4: Lecture 4 (Geometric Priors II) - Joan Bruna
theme: Geometric Deep Learning Starts By Rejecting Unstructured Learning
subtheme: Geometric priors are the repair strategy, not a decorative add-on
discussion: The second priors lecture sharpens the tradeoff between expressivity and bias. The discussion is useful because it stops structure from sounding like dogma and instead presents it as disciplined restriction in service of generalization.

title: Session 5: Lecture 5 (Graphs & Sets) - Petar Veličković
theme: Domains Differ, So The Operators Have To Differ
discussion: The graphs-and-sets lecture marks the transition from motivation into operator design. It shows that the field becomes concrete only when the geometry of the domain dictates what aggregation is allowed.

title: Session 6: Lecture 6 (Graphs & Sets II) - Petar Veličković
theme: Domains Differ, So The Operators Have To Differ
subtheme: Graphs require relation-aware locality and message passing
discussion: Graphs & Sets II is a pressure test for plain message passing. The discussion is valuable because several later frontier methods make sense only after you see where ordinary graph models fail to distinguish structure.

title: Session 7: Lecture 7 (Grids) - Joan Bruna
theme: Domains Differ, So The Operators Have To Differ
subtheme: Grids recover classical convolution as one structured special case
discussion: The grids lecture repositions convolution inside a broader conceptual map. That is important pedagogically because it stops CNN intuition from dominating domains where grid assumptions do not hold.

title: Session 8: Lecture 8 (Groups & Homogeneous spaces) - Taco Cohen
theme: Symmetry Is The Central Language For Encoding Structure
subtheme: Groups and homogeneous spaces make global symmetry computational
discussion: The groups lecture is the course's most explicit statement that symmetry can be operationalized mathematically. It connects the intuitive desire for structured behavior to a formal recipe for operator construction.

title: Session 9: Lecture 9 (Manifolds) - Michael Bronstein
theme: Manifolds And Local Frames Generalize Euclidean Intuition
subtheme: Manifolds turn curved spaces into first-class learning domains
discussion: The manifolds lecture matters because it breaks the habit of assuming the ambient Euclidean space tells the whole story. Bronstein keeps returning attention to intrinsic geometry and local structure.

title: Session 10: Lecture 10 (Gauges) - Taco Cohen
theme: Manifolds And Local Frames Generalize Euclidean Intuition
subtheme: Gauge equivariance replaces one global frame with compatible local ones
discussion: Gauge equivariance is the point where the course becomes genuinely local. The key discussion is not only about symmetry, but about compatibility between overlapping local descriptions when no single frame is privileged.

title: Session 11: Lecture 11 (Beyond Groups) - Petar Veličković
theme: Manifolds And Local Frames Generalize Euclidean Intuition
subtheme: Beyond-groups thinking asks what other organizing structures matter
discussion: Beyond Groups keeps the course intellectually open. Instead of declaring the job finished with groups, the lecture asks what other structures deserve to play the same organizing role for harder domains.

title: Session 12: Lecture 12 (Applications & Trends) - Michael Bronstein
theme: The Frontier Is Measured By Working Applications, Not Only Theory
subtheme: Applications and trends turn the blueprint into a research agenda
discussion: Applications & Trends is less a recap than a positioning statement. It shows where the blueprint has worked, where the theory is still incomplete, and why the field remains an active research frontier.

title: Session 13: Seminar 1 (Physics-based GNNs) - Francesco Di Giovanni
theme: The Frontier Is Measured By Working Applications, Not Only Theory
subtheme: Scientific and expressive graph variants push beyond vanilla message passing
discussion: The physics-based GNN seminar is the course's scientific credibility check. It demonstrates that structure-aware graph modeling is not just elegant abstraction, but a usable tool for systems governed by known interaction laws.

title: Session 14: Seminar 2 (Subgraph GNNs) - Fabrizio Frasca
theme: The Frontier Is Measured By Working Applications, Not Only Theory
subtheme: Scientific and expressive graph variants push beyond vanilla message passing
discussion: Subgraph GNNs are discussed as an expressivity repair strategy. The seminar matters because it makes the limitations of vanilla message passing concrete rather than merely theoretical.

title: Session 15: Seminar 3 (Equivariance in ML) - Geordie Williamson
theme: The Frontier Is Measured By Working Applications, Not Only Theory
subtheme: Equivariance and protein structure show the payoff of getting geometry right
discussion: The equivariance seminar broadens the audience's intuition for when transformation-aware learning is worth the complexity. It reinforces symmetry as a durable design idea rather than a one-lecture curiosity.

title: Session 16: Seminar 4 (Neural Sheaf Diffusion) - Cristian Bodnar
theme: The Frontier Is Measured By Working Applications, Not Only Theory
subtheme: Scientific and expressive graph variants push beyond vanilla message passing
discussion: Neural sheaf diffusion pushes the frontier into richer local-to-global consistency frameworks. It is a good example of how the field expands when classical graph primitives no longer feel expressive enough.

title: Session 17: Seminar 5 (AlphaFold) - Russ Bates
theme: The Frontier Is Measured By Working Applications, Not Only Theory
subtheme: Equivariance and protein structure show the payoff of getting geometry right
discussion: The AlphaFold seminar functions as the capstone application. It shows why the course is ultimately about matching inductive bias to domain reality well enough to unlock otherwise unreachable performance.
